healthcareSystem: Government-funded public healthcare through the Republic of Nauru Hospital (RON Hospital). Free for citizens but very limited in scope. The island has one hospital with basic capabilities only.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is extremely limited. RON Hospital provides basic emergency and primary care but lacks specialist services, advanced imaging, and surgical capabilities. Serious conditions require medical evacuation to Australia. High rates of diabetes and obesity affect the population.
pharmacyHours: RON Hospital pharmacy operates during business hours (Mon-Fri 8am-4pm). No private pharmacies on the island.
pharmacyTips: The hospital pharmacy is the only source of medications. Supply is limited and intermittent. Bring all necessary medications from home in quantities to last your entire stay plus extra.
prescriptionRules: Limited prescription system. The hospital pharmacy dispenses medications based on doctor consultations. Foreign prescriptions may not be recognized — bring sufficient supplies from home.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled narcotics
restrictedMeds.note: Narcotic medications are controlled. Carry a doctor's letter and original prescriptions.

bringDocumentation: Carry a comprehensive doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Bring all medications in original packaging with quantities for your entire stay plus reserves.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is absolutely essential. Evacuation to Australia is the only option for serious conditions and can cost $30,000-100,000+. Verify your policy covers remote Pacific island evacuations.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for entry. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Dengue fever risk exists. No malaria on the island.

waterNotes: Tap water is not reliably safe. The island relies on desalination and rainwater collection. Drink bottled water or boil tap water. Water supply can be intermittent.
foodSafetyTips: Most food is imported and generally safe from stores. Limited fresh produce. Eat freshly prepared foods. Be cautious with fish due to ciguatera poisoning risk in reef fish.
medicalTourismNote: Nauru is not a medical tourism destination. Nauruans frequently travel to Australia for medical care.
sources: Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
metaDescription: Health guide for Nauru. Emergency numbers, RON Hospital info, travel insurance, medical evacuation to Australia, and health tips for travelers.

hospitals.name: Republic of Nauru Hospital (RON Hospital)
hospitals.notes: The only hospital on the island. Provides basic emergency care, general medicine, and maternity services. Limited diagnostic equipment. English is an official language.

dentalCare.availability: Basic dental services available at RON Hospital. One or two dentists serve the entire island.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is very basic. Only extractions and simple procedures available. No orthodontics or cosmetic dentistry.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: RON Hospital can handle dental emergencies during business hours. For anything beyond basic extractions, evacuation to Australia is necessary.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: Contact your embassy or International SOS
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are minimal. The hospital has limited counseling capacity. Pre-arrange remote therapy options before traveling.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Very limited accessibility infrastructure on this small island nation.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: RON Hospital has basic wheelchair access but limited facilities.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No public transportation system. Roads are flat but not designed for wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Nauru is a small, relatively flat island. Private vehicle transport is essential. Accommodation options are very limited and may not be accessible.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited COVID testing available at RON Hospital.
covidStatus.notes: Healthcare capacity is very limited. A respiratory illness outbreak could overwhelm the single hospital.

insuranceClaimProcess: RON Hospital can provide basic receipts and medical reports in English. Payment may be required for foreign visitors. Keep all documentation for insurance claims. Claims must be filed with your insurer after departure.

commonCosts.note: Nauru uses the Australian dollar. Costs are moderate but services are extremely limited. Complex care requires evacuation.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation is the only option for serious conditions. Charter flights from Nauru to Australia take 4-5 hours. The island's small airstrip limits aircraft size. Evacuation logistics can take 24-48 hours to arrange.
